REPORT OF THE RITUAL COMMITTEE
To th e M.".

w:. Grand Lodge of California:

We, the Committee on Ritual, submit the following report:
The Ritual Committee has spared no effort to put into successful operation
the .action adopted by Grand Lodge in 1934 relative to ritualistic instruction.
The Grand Lecturer, in his report, has detailed the work of the committee
as its members have traveled throughout the length and breadth of the jurisdiction. The time given to the work, the number of sessions held with Inspectors
and the economy with which the plan has been administered, need no further
comment here.
During the course of the year many suggestions for ritual changes have
been presented to the committee by officers of Lodges, by Inspectors and by the
committee members. All these suggestions have received careful consideration
but no change in the language of the three degrees has been adopted by the
·
present committee.
In the interest of clarification of meaning and of simplification in performance some rearrangement in parts of the floor work of the three degrees has
been worke? out. This rearrangement has been studied over a period of many
months until now a final arrangement has been perfected for the coming year.
The floor work of all degrees has been imparted to the Inspectors in schools
of instruction. The floor work of the third degree (which is the portion most
affected) was exemplified for all the members of Grand Lodge on Wednesday
evening, October 9, 1935, by officers of California Lodge No. I. The work as
exemplified is to be effective immediately. No further rearrangement will be
made during the coming year.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

571

:we therefore offer the following resolution and move its adoption: That
the present plan of ritualistic instruction be continued for the ensuing year.
LESLIE E. Wooo, .
SIDNEY K. LEHMAN,
LLOYD E. WILSON.

The report, including the resolution, was adopted.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON GRAND LECTURER'S
REPORT
To the M.". W.". Grand Lodge of California:

The committe to whom the report of the Grand Lecturer was referred begs
leave to submit the following :
The report which · the Grand Lecturer ·presented covers his stewardship for
the last twelve months. Realizing the short period that he has held this office,
and the vast amount of work which he has accomplished, we cannot help but
marvel at his achievements.
The high standard of proficiency achieved by the various Lodges in the
ritualistic work is visible evidence, not only to the skill and ability of the Grand
Lecturer, but of the generous cooperation of the Assistant Grand Lecturers and
the Inspectors.
We note with great satisfaction that each lnspectorial District in the
jurisdiction (except those in the Hawaiian Islands) has been .instructed in the
ritual from two to five times during the year. We heartily commend these
Assistant Grand Lecturers, Oscar L. Harris, Lloyd E. Wilson, Chester .. H .
Warlow and Sidney K. Lehman, for their untiring efforts and the assistance
·
they have given the Inspectors.
No one can question but that the ritual is the very foundation or' our
Masonic structure, and that from it emanates the principles of our Order. We
must maintain its perfection. We heartily concur in the idea of the ritual being
perpetuated through a Grand Lecturer and four Assistants.
Under this method of teaching the ritual, more schools of instruction are
held, and smaller attendance at the meetings means more individual instruction
and greater proficiency acquired by the officers.
Criticism has been offered that only officers are instructed in the ritual
under this revised plan. We see no reason why any Brother interested in
learning the ritual· should not attend the schools of instruction.
No changes have' been made in the ritual, ·b ut a few changes have been
. made in the floor work. Commendations and criticisms o.£ these changes have
bee? recei".ed. Progress and development can come only .!Ji.rqµg-1}, trial and expenmentat10n. We feel that these changes are entitled to a fai; ,trial and that
beneficial results are bound to come. However, 'we recommend that no further
changes be made during the coming year.
We feel that much of the success of this plan has been due to the valuable
assistance rendered by Past Grand Master Dana R. \Veller. His long service
on the Ritual Committee, and his thorough understanding of the work, has
cleared the skies and made a difficult task more easily performed.
We are happy to note that the condition of the Lodges is improving and
that dues are coming in more readily, also, that more time is being devoted to
fellowship and education.
·
It is gratifying to find the Officers' Associations functioning smoothly and
the officers becoming better informed in law and procedure.
We commend the Grand Lecturer in his method of propounding questions
to the Masters and Wardens-elect to ascertain their knowledge of the Constitution .and Regulations governing their Lodges.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

572

We sincerely commend the Grand Lecturer in his admonition "that we
should endeavor to act with the greatest dignity and decorum" at all public
ceremonies. A Masonic burial is a sacred duty, and should be performed with
· dignity, reverence and respect. It is well that a brother amply qualified should
discharge this important trust.
The Grand Lecturer and his Assistant Grand Lecturers journeyed more
than seventeen thousand miles during the year at a total cost of less than
$1,800.00. We congratulate them on the saving to Grand Lodge of more than
$5,000.00 over the old plan.
Our Grand Lectu~r has made many Lodge visitations this year, installing
the officers, presenting fifty year buttons, and giving educational talks. His
forcible manner, his kindly advice and counsel, and his loyalty to his trust have
·
endeared him in the hearts of those fortunate enough to know him.

Limitation of Relief
Your conunittee has considered the resolution of Brother Mallachowitz,
reading as follows :
"That wherever in the Constitution relief is mentioned, in sections 90, 163
and others, the clause 'insofar as it may do so without serious injury to itself/
be added."
Section 90 of our Constitution now provides that "Each Lodge shall see
to it, even if it require all of its funds and property, that the needy brethren
of its own membership and neighborhood are not suffered to want or to be made
a burden to others." This is a drastic provision of our law and probably
should be amended, as indicated by the resolution of Brother Mallachowitz, btit
we are · of the opinion that this entire subject should be considered in conneetion
with the resolution of Brother Wesley Kergan at the next annual communication, and we so recommend.

The report was adopted.

Your .Conunittee on Policy and General Purposes is in hearty accord with

issued to Past Masters of this jurisdiction, and recommend the adoption of the
resolution.

88 of the Constitution, which permits a Lodge in its discretion to appropriate
from its funds any amount for a testimonial for its retiring Master, the Lodge
may as such a testimonial purchase for him a life membership in the Lodge.
In the opinion of the committee these rulings, as above recited, are correct, and
we recommend their approval.
In connection with the purchase of life membership testimonials, we, however, emphasize the necessity under section 129 of the Constitution for the
transfer by the Lodge from its general fund to its life membership fund of the
amount required in its case for the purchase of a life membership, and the
necessity for the inclusion of that amount in its life membership investments
which are permanently retained, and which are not subject to use for charity or
other general purposes, even in an emergency. We also suggest the inadvisability of such a practice on the part of any Lodge whose membership is
limited, or whose sources of income for general purposes are either restricted ot
subject to demands which in time of financial stringency render adequate
financing difficult. In the case of a small Lodge an . undue percentage of its
members may be transferred to the life membership class, and frequently the
returns from investments of the life membership fund are inadequate to cover.
a proper proportion of general expense; for the same reason the purchase of an
tindue number of life mem!Jerships for retiring Masters may prove embarrassing to a Lodge whose finances, either ordinarily or in time of emergency, require
careful administration.

Communism
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes has given careful consideration to the resolution presented by the Masters and Wardens of the East
. Bay Lodges relative to communism. We heartily commend and endorse the
matters contained therein, but are of opinion that it would be impolitic for
the Grand Lodge to go on public record in matters that might be construed
as be!ng politically partisan. Last year this Grand Lodge adopted resolutions
pledgmg the Masons and Masonry of this jurisdiction to fealty to government
and we feel that a reaffirmation in the language of the proposed resolution i~
unnecessary. We therefore recommend that the resolution be not made o{
record.

otherwise, to remit the dues of any of its members for any stat~d period, or in
advance, except as to one who has been a member of a Lodge in good standing
in t~is jurisdiction for a period of forty years or more, but that it may annually
remit the accru~ dues of those of its members who render special service to
the Lodge, or who are unable to pay them. He further holds that under section

Report adopted.
Forty-Year Memben
Your Committee on Jurisprudence, with the approval of the Committee on
Policy and General Purposes, proposes and recommends the following amendment to the Constitution of the Grand Lodge, to-wit:
Amend Section No. 128 thereof by substituting the following for the
language now contained in said section immediately following the word "filing,"
at the end of the third sentence of said section:
. "No Lodge shall remit the dues of its members or any of them for any
stated period or in advance ; but it may annually remit the accrued dues of those
of its members who render special service for the Lodge or who are unable to
pay them. Provided, nevertheless, that by special resolution, applicable only to
the particular member involved, a Lodge may, in advance or otherwise, remit
the dues of any member who shall have been a member in good standing in this
jurisdiction for forty years or more, and who in the sound judgment of the
Lodge, should, by reason of some misfortune, inability or other good cause, be
exempt from the payment of dues. No Lodge shall levy any extra assessment
on its members."

The report was adopted and section 128 of the Constitution
was amended by a five-sixths vote.
Acacia Lodge No. 438
Your Committee on Jurisprudence approved decision No. 19, as set out in
the Message of the Grand Master. That decision related to the J>Uspension of
the Master and the arrest of · the charter of Acacia Lodge No. 438. We recommend that the matter of the arrest of the charter and the suspension of the

the warring factions in the Lodge if possible, and report its findings and conclusions to the Grand Master ; that the Grand Master be empowered to continue the charter under arrest or to surrender it again to the Lodge and to
reinstate the Master, if in his judgment such should be done.

Commercial Activities of Lodges
The Committee on Jurisprudence has had referred to it a resolution from
the Committee on Policy and General Purposes, contained in the proceedings
of the Grand Lodge of California, for the year 1932, on page 323 thereof,
referring to commercial activities of Lodges, and requesting this committee to
prepare the necessary legislation whereby the policy expressed in that resolution
should be made effective. This resolution having again been called to our attention, we now propose the following amendment to the Constitution :
That section 127 of the Constitution be amended by inserting therein after
the se!1tence concluding with the words, "however worthy it may be," the
following:
·
"Nor shall any Lodge sponsor, or by resolution or otherwise sanction or
permit the use of the name of the Lodge in connection with, or for the pur~ose
of furthering any financial undertaking, or commercial venture whether for
profit or not, which shall not have been approved by the Grand Master, nor
shall any member of any Lodge be permitted to do so except in his individual
capacity, and without the use of the name of the Lodge."
We recommend the adoption of the foregoing amendment.

Dispensations Issued
Your Committee on Jurisprudence has examined the records of the issuance of dispensations for various purposes and approval of resolutions establishing life memberships ·by the Grand Master, and find same to be in
accordance with our law.
We, therefore, recommend that the action of the Grand Master in that
respect be approved.

Report of the committee was adopted, and section 127 of the

Purchase of Photographs of Past Masters
The Most Worshipful Grand Master ruled that a Lodge was without power
to use any Lodge funds wherewith to purchase photographs of portraits of its
Past Masters '.'to be placed in a fireproof safe to be used in the event the
originals were lost," and that the cost of the same "should be supplied if at all
· '
by individual contributions."
'
. The ruling was based upon a decision of Grand Master Preston, (1896), in
which he held, Grand Lodge approving, that "Lodge funds cannot be used to
purchase jewels for retiring officers, or to purchase portraits of such officers
to ornament the wall on a Lodge room."
Since the ruling in 1896, the Constitution of the Grand Lodge has been
amended to permit the use of Lodge funds in payment of the "necessary expenses" of the Lodge, and in "any amount for the purchase of a testimonial
for the retiring Master."
·
We think a reasonable construction of the Constitution will permit of the
purchase from its general fund of photographs of Past Masters, in order that
such photographs may be put in a safe' place for preservation. Such would not
be 1issimilar to the purchase of appropriate books of record, or of a photostatic copy of the same, if deemed necessary and desirable, for the proper
perpetuation of the history of the Lodge. It might reasonably be construed in
aid of an appropriate "testimonial" to the retired Masters.
As long as an expense incurred by a Lodge is reasonably necessary to the
proper performance of its duty as an instrumentality of Free Masonry, we
think, under existing Constitutional provisions, such expense may not be subjected to interdiction. If the Lodge deemed the expenditures for the photographs in question reasonably necessary for the proper perpetuation of its
Masonic re<."ords,. which we must assume it did so conclude, we feel that we
may not merely as a matter of Masonic law, overrule such conclusion.
Furthermore, we cannot say that the Lodge would not be reasonably engaged in "promoting fraternal intercourse" to provide its archives with the
photographs referred to. Such being the case, under section 89 of the Constitution, the 20 per cent social fund would be available, and therefore to do
the thing referred to in the Grand Master's ruling, the Lodge would not be
driven to the necessity of securing '"individual contdbutions."
We recommend that decision No. 7 be not approved.

Report was adopted.

Report was adopted.
Dispensations to Act on Rejected Applicants
Your Committee on Jurisprudence, to which was referred decision No. 11
of the Grand Master, reports as follows:
Under section 43, subdivision 4th, the Grand Master has power to grant
dispensations to .receive and act upon the petitions of rejected applicants for the
degrees, within less than the twelve months prescribed in section 97 under the
regulations provided in section 106. The Grand Master has no authority to
issue a dispensation to reballot upon the petition on which the candidate has
been rejected; a new petition must be filed.
The Grand Master ruled that he had exercised 'the discretion with which
he was vested only when there was good reason to believe that a mistake had
been made, or other extraordinary circumstances existed, and that a showing
should be made to the Grand Master of the reason for granting the dispensation.
· In this we believe the Grand Master acted within the power granted him.
]OHN D. MURPHEY, Chairman.

REPORT OF BOARD OF CONTROL
To the M.'. w:. Grand Lodge of California:
Your Board of Control is pleased to submit the annual report of its
activities during the Masonic year.
· Before doing so, however, it wishes to call to the attention of our Brethren
the irreparable loss that has been sustained, by Masonry in general and the
Board of Control in particular, in the passing of the Board's be!Oved Chairman,
counsellor and self-sacrificing friend, Brother David J. Reese. His guiding
spirit seems to ·be with us in our deliberations and the excellent procedure
originated during his regime is being continued. Time cannot eradicate the
fond love and veneration which remains in our hearts for him.
His i:>ersonality and ability were recognized nationally as well as locally.
Brother Lewis E. Smith, Past Grand Master of the Grand Lodge of Nebraska
and President of the Masonic Relief Association of the United States and
Canada, wrote from Omaha, Neb.:
"M.'. w:. Brother Reese made a wonderful impression at our meeting
in Cincinnati. I do not know of any man who ever attended just one of
our association meetings, who created such a fine impression, and who won
the admiration of so many of the brethren, as did Brother Reese."

Brother E. E. Axtell, Secretary of the Masonic Relief Association of the
United States and Canada, wrote from Buffalo, N. Y.:
"The late lamented Brother David J. Reese practically stole the Convention two years ago, both by his lovable personality and the magnificent
paper he read covering the formation and activities of your Board, and I
assure you that we all felt a deep personal loss in his passing."
"God's finger touched him, and he slept."

The Board also suffered a severe loss in the passing of Brother Auguste F.
Brinkman shortly after his appointment. There was every indication that he
would have ·been a very valuable acquisition to the Board.
Brother Frank Tade, of Sacramento Lodge No. 40, Sacramento, was appointed by the Most Worshipful Grand Master, to replace Brother Brinlanan.
Brother Tade has already shown an unusual aptitude for the work and will be
a wise counsellor in our deliberations.
There has been a splendid cooperation with the Board of Control by the
Boards of Relief and the individual Lodges, and this has brought about a
decided reduction not only in the number of cases but also in the number of
cases of an apparently uncollectible nature that it has been necessary to refer
t-0 the Board; very valuable suggestions and assistance have also been rendered by Secretaries of the Boards of Relief and Lodges. There has been
better understanding and more friendly contact between the Board of Control
of our Grand Lodge and the leaders in · relief work in other jurisdictions,
brought about mainly ·by the representative of our Board of Control attending
the convention of the Masonic Relief Association of the United States and
Canada, in 1933.
The final result has been that the Grand Lodge of California is being
called upon for a decreased amount for reimbursements each year notwithstanding the fact that the Boards of Relief and Lodges have maintained the
real spirit of Masonry in handling their various requests for relief.

year for action, while a number of cases are still carried forward from previous years.

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
To the M:. w:. Grand Lodge of California:
Your Committee on Finance begs leave to submit the following report·
Reimbursement of Boards of Relief
Your 'committee has examined the reports of the Board of Control on Reimbursement of Boards of Relief, and Masonic Employment Service. The
report is complete and displays the great amount of care the Board has exercised,
and the tremend-0us amount of work that it has done. We have nothing but
words of commendation for the work of this committee. It is saving the Grand
Lodge money.
The report of the Board recommends reimbursements to Boaras of Relid~
as follows :
·
·
San Francisco Board of Relief.. ..........................................$ 436.00
Los Angeles Board of Relief............................................. . 120.75
East Bay Board of Relief... ..............................................:.. 430.14
Cupertino Lodge No. 510......................................................
61.75
Laguna Beach Lodge No. 572.............................:..............
50.00
Total...............................:...............:....................$1,098.64
We offer t·he following resolution and recommend its adoption :
Resolt'ed, That the sum of $1,098.64 be and is hereby appropriated from th,·
funds of Grand Lodge to reimburse Boards of Relief and the two Lodges in tllt'
amounts as set out above.
Masonic Employment Service
Your committee, upon the recommendation of the Board of Control, offers
the following resolution and recommends its adoption:
Resolved, That the sum of $10,800.00 be and is hereby appropriated from the
funds of Grand Lodge, to be divided into the following donations to assist in
maintaining Employment Bureaus:
San Francisco Employment Service................................$ 2,400.00
East Bay Employment Service........................................ 2,400.00
Los Angeles Employment Service.................................... 3,300.00
San Diego Employment Service................:................... _..
800.00
Long Beach Employment Service.................................... 1,500.00
Sacramento Employment Service....................................
400.00
Total.. .................:..............................................$10,800.00
Reports of Grand Officers
The reports of the Grand Treasurer and Grand Secretary have been examined by this committee. The reports of both of these efficient officers display
great care and ability in handling the business of Grand Lodge. Your committee
has nothing but words of comme£Jdation and appreciation for their splendid
work.
The Grand Treasurer is performing a service for this grand body that
little attention has been given to, and yet it is of great importance. The service
referred to is the investment of the funds of Grand Lodge in various securities.
Grand Lodge has investments in securities through the Endowment Fund and
surplus Grand Lodge funds in excess of $1,000,000. To keep these funds carefully and properly invested, requires constant watching and rare judgment.
Both the Endowment Board and the Trustees of the Homes have committees to assist the Grand Treasurer in the performance of this important

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

593

function. The Grand Treasurer, however, is giving this requirement constant
scrutiny, arid with little attention from Grand Lodge on its importance.
The committee feels the Grand Treasurer is entitled to particular mention
and commendation for this service.
Grand Lodge Per Capita
The Constitution provides for the levying of a per capita of 50c to provide
for the expenses of Grand Lodge and its various committees. As will be noted
by the Budget, which is being submitted with this report, the revenue derived
from this source, together with other revenues coming to Grand Lodge, will
not be sufficient to provide for Grand Lodge activities for this coming year. The
differem:e ~s so small, however, that we feel unwilling to provide for any ad. ditional levy. The difference can be paid from the surplus accumulated from
previous years.
· The Constitution also provides for a per capita levy of 50c fo r .the Building Fund of Masonic Homes. In addition to this Building Fund and the other
revenues coming to the Homes, the H omes Trustees have recommended
the levying of an additional per capita of 75c for the maintenance of our two
Homes. Your committee is in accord with this request, and, therefore, offers the
following resolution and recommends its adoption.
Resolved, That a per capita of 75c per member be levied, and when paid,
shall be paid by the Grand Secretary to the Trustees of the H omes, for the
operation and maintenance expenses of the Homes.
Masonic Club Houses of the University of California at Berkeley and
Los Angeles
Your committee ·has reviewed the reports of the Trustees of these two Club
Houses, together with Public Accountants' reports on their accounts. These
reports indicate to your committee that great care is being exercised by the
Trustees of these two .Masonic activities, in their management and the spending
of the money necessary for their maintenance.
In discussing this activity the Trustees are loud in their praise of the good
that these two clubs are accomplishing. \ Ve also want to commend the Trustees
for the detail ofl the Budgets which they have presented. It would seem to your
committee that the requests which the Trustees make for funds for the continuation of these activities for this coming year, are quite reasonable. Your
committee, therefore, offers the following resolution and recommends its
adoption:
Resolved, That the sum of $14,000.00 be appropriated from the funds of
Grand Lodge, for the support of the Masonic Club Houses, $7,000.00 thereof to
be paid to the Trustees of the Masonic Club House at Berkeley, and $7,000.00
thereof to be paid to the Trustees of the Masonic Club House at Los Angeles.

A request has been received from Humboldt Lodge that the dues which
they owe for the year 1934 be remitted, and one from Yorba Linda Lodge, that
the balance they owe for dues for the year 1932, also be remitted. Your committee finds on inquiry that conditions in both of these communities have materially improved and that the outlook for the future for the communities, as
well as from a Masonic way, is good. It also must be borne in mind that the
remission of dues of any Lodge, throws an additional burden on other Lodges.
We, therefore, recommend that the request of these two Lodges be denied, and
that further time be given them for the payment of the balance .which they owe
on Grand Lodge dues.
We make a similar recommendation for Larchmont Lodge, No. 614, and
Concord Lodge, No. 117. For those four Lodges which have been unable to
pay their 1935 dues, we propose the following resolution and recommend its
adoption:

Resolved, That each of the subordinate Lodges whose names are set out
above, execute notes in favor of the Grand Lodge for the amount due by each
of the said l:.odges in payment of said Grand Lodge dues, said notes to come due
on or before six months from date and bear interest at the rate of four percent
per annum.
Audit of Accounts
In accordance with the policy heretofore pursued by this committee, your
committee again employed the firm of Ruckstell and Land, Certified Public Accountants, to examine the books and records of the Grand Secretary-the Grand
Treasurer, the Masonic Homes of California, and the Endowment Fund. The
reports of this firm's examination on all of these records have been filed with
your committee. The report indicates that all records are correct and in proper
shape.
Travel Expenses of Grand Master
Your committee has given consideration to an appropriation to cover the
traveling expenses of the Grand Master for this coming year. We note that for
the year just closing, as well as the previous year, the entire appropriation made
for this purpose, has not been used. The committee is of the opinion, however,
that no reduction should be made in the appropriation for this purpose. We,
therefore, offer the following resolution and recommend its adoption:

Resolved, That the sum of $3,500.00 be, and the same is hereby appropriated
from the funds of Grand Lodge, to pay the traveling expenses of the Grand
Master during the coming Masonic year.

Masonic Homes Endowment Board
Your committee has examined the report of the activities of the Masonic
·Homes Endowment Board for the past year wherein the Board shows the collection of approximately $57,000. The expense of this collection was covered
by an appropriation of $6,000 by Grand Lodge at its annual communication in
1934. Your committee is of the opinion that the Masonic H omes Endowment
Board should continue their splendid effort to create a substantial endowment
fund, not only as a tribute to our departed brother, W. P . Jeffries, but ultimately looking toward the goal of relieving Grand Lodge and the constituent
Lodges of the cost of maintaining our Masonic Homes. Your committee having
in mind the reduction of expense wherever possible and giving favorable consideration to the request of the Masonic H omes Endowment Board, offer the
following resolution and recommends its adoption:
Resolved, That the sum of $4,000 be and is hereby appropriated from the
funds of Grand Lodge to be paid to the Masonic Homes Endowment Board
for its expenses for the year ending July 31, 1936.
Budget
In analyzing the report of the Grand Secretary as to receipts and disburse· ments for the year ending July 31, 1935, we find that the income received was
about $1,000.00 over the amount included in the budget at the last annual com·munication. However, the total disbursements are in excess of the amounts budgeted, and also in excess of income received.
Total expenditures, after allowing for offsetting items, amounted to approximately $90,000.00, or about $6,000.00 in excess of the budget figures, and
about $8,500.00 in excess of the actual income for the same period. · This difference is more than accounted for by the two items of relief-Grand Masters
relief of $5,701.14 exceeding the budget by $700.00, and reimbursement of the
Masonic H omes in the amount of $6,342.09, the amount paid for outside relief
chargeable to Grand Lodge, and for which no amount was set up in the budget.
It 'is very difficult to budget relief expenditures, but your committee feels .
that some estimate should be made, and it ·has therefore included both items in
the budget for next year, which i~ as follows:

operating, which should lighten the relief burden. One of the most important
of these is the new old age pension law just passed by the legislature.

Proposed Recommendations of Amendments to Constitution Proposed by
Committee on Accounts
The resolutions presented by the Committee on Accounts proposing altering
sections 37-E and 37-K, which sections provide for the payments of expenses
incurred by the members of the Board of Control and of the Endowment
Board, have been given consideration by your committee. The committee understands the purport of these two changes is to require that the expenses of these
two boards will have to be audited by the Accounts Committee before they are
in proper shape for payment. While this will entail some additional trouble and
delay by these two boards in securing the payment of expenses incurred, yet it
would seem to this committee that this scrutiny is in the line of additional care
·
..
and economy of expenses.
We, therefore, raise no objection to these proposed changes in the Constitution. It is to be noted, however, that the proposed amendments eliminate

A~ 5 :15 o'clock Grand Lodge was called off until 9 :30 Friday

A proposed plan for the submission of information to Lodges,
as originally proposed by the resolution of Brother Donovan,
having been made special order for consideration at this time, the
following resolution was presented :
To the M.'. W.'. Grand Lodge of California:
Resolved, that all resolutions and proposed legislation to be presented for
consideration of Grand Lodge shall be in the hands of the Grand Secretary
sixty days prior to any annual communication of Grand Lodge, and all other
resolutions or p(oposed legislation presented during the period sixty days immediately prior to the annual communication of Grand Lodge, or during sessions
of Grand Lodge, shall be acted upon if a two-thirds vote of the members
present at Grand Lodge so direct, providing further that the Grand Secretary
be instructed to cause a short summary of all such resolutions and proposed
ltgislation in his hands, sixty days before the annual communication of Grand
Lodge, to be compiled and printed in leaflet form, and there shall be included
therein decisions. of the Grand Master as then rendered and such recommendations as to proposed legislation as the Grand Master may ·be prepared to present,

each subordinate Lodge in this jurisdiction copy of said leaflet prior to the
stated meeting of such subordinate Lodge immediately preceding the annual
communication of Grand Lodge.
